_note: E4 executive/PA whaling attack fragment (wave 4, opus48 slot). A fragment of the `social` block; the full-episode shell copies these keys into scenarios/awareness_e4_*/scenario.json.erb and the defend-only/check shells leave the attack out. All companies and people are fictional (BRAND_SET.md, Merrin & Sallow Architects). The learner, a junior red-teamer on an authorised Merrin & Sallow exercise, impersonates managing partner Catherine Merrin while she is travelling and out of contact, and emails her PA, Tomás Carvalho (phish target `exec_pa`), to push through an urgent payment that bypasses finance. No payload, no link, no attachment: the whole trick is a trusted name on a freemail address plus a travel excuse. The audio half of E4 (the 'cloned voice' voice note and call) lives in the E4 defend set, not here, and ships as transcript stand-ins on the `voicemail` kind with an `audio.clipId` named but not yet made (PHASE7_PACKETS.md wave 4, held packets P7-Z1/P7-Z2). The attack beat itself has no audio. See the Docs hand-off in the report for the globals the shell must declare and the tells a good send stores for the flip.

ms_managing_partner.text: Catherine Merrin is the managing partner at Merrin & Sallow and signs off the practice's spending.
ms_managing_partner.subject: catherine
ms_managing_partner.reduceNote: Naming who at the top can authorise money hands an attacker the identity whose authority is worth borrowing.

ms_pa_name.text: Tomás Carvalho is Catherine Merrin's executive assistant and runs her diary and day-to-day payments while she travels.
ms_pa_name.subject: tomas
ms_pa_name.reduceNote: Publishing who handles an executive's diary and payments tells an attacker exactly whom to send the request to.

ms_exec_calendar.text: The events page shows Catherine Merrin is speaking at the Lisbon Design Forum this week, flying out Tuesday morning and back Thursday.
ms_exec_calendar.subject: catherine
ms_exec_calendar.reduceNote: A public diary tells an attacker when the executive is unreachable and gives a believable reason to be emailing on the move.

ms_exec_travel_email.text: Catherine's speaker bio says that while she is travelling she takes urgent enquiries at catherine.merrin@inboxly.example.
ms_exec_travel_email.subject: catherine
ms_exec_travel_email.reduceNote: An executive's personal or travel email in public lets an attacker send as a name staff trust, on a channel nobody can check against the company address book.

ms_travel_post.text: Catherine posted that she is flying to Lisbon for the Design Forum this week, giving her flight time, and will be barely online until Thursday.
ms_travel_post.subject: catherine
ms_travel_post.reduceNote: A post confirming the executive is away and distracted gives the attacker both the window and the urgency to work with.

ms_pretext_pay_now.text: I'm about to board for {trip} and I'll have no signal for a few hours. There's a contractor invoice that has to be settled today or we lose the slot. Can you push it through from the practice account? Keep it between us for now, no need to trouble finance, and I'll square it with them when I land.

ms_pretext_pay_calm.text: I'm away at {trip} this week. There's a contractor invoice to settle from the practice account when you get a chance this week, nothing urgent. I'll confirm it with finance when I'm back.

ms_pretext_diary.text: When you get a moment, could you send me next week's diary?

ms_ask_confirm.text: Drop me a line here once it's gone through.

ms_ask_calm.text: No rush, let me know once it's sorted.

seededMessages.subject: Authorised exercise: Merrin & Sallow
seededMessages.body:
Hello,

This is the authorised Merrin & Sallow exercise. In scope: this inbox and the people on it. Research the partner and her PA, then write one message. Nothing leaves this account.

Red team lead

blocks.text: This week: Catherine Merrin speaks at the Lisbon Design Forum (Wednesday 10:00), flying out Tuesday at 09:55 and home Thursday evening.
Speaker: Catherine Merrin. While she is travelling, urgent enquiries reach her at catherine.merrin@inboxly.example.

posts.text: Off to Lisbon Tuesday for the Design Forum — speaking Wednesday morning, home Thursday. 09:55 flight out. Barely online till then.
The new footbridge model came back from the workshop. Worth every late night.

primedFor.story: a payment the managing partner has personally asked for while she is travelling and out of contact

open.fail: Nothing about the sender or the subject made him open it.

senderTrust.fail: He does not act on money from a stranger. The request has to look like it is from Catherine.

pretextRelevant.pass: ✓ Fits a trip he knows she is on
pretextRelevant.fail: No trip he can match this to, so a message out of the blue reads as odd rather than something she'd send while she's away.

replies.landed: Will do, Catherine. I'll get it paid this afternoon and keep it off the finance thread. Safe travels.
replies.missed: Before I pay anything I'll confirm it with Catherine on her usual number, or check with finance. Nothing goes out until then.

hints: Whose name would make the PA act on a payment without checking?
What trip is she publicly on this week, so an email from the road reads as expected?
Set the From line to Catherine's name and her travel email, and tie the message to the Lisbon Design Forum.
